chapter: Life on the road and in the Webb band's book
title: Cleaning and repairing horns on tour
summary: The musicians cleaned their own horns nightly and had a repairman restore a horn after a trunk was dropped on it.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Cleaning the horn, did you save that for --
No, we cleaned our own horns, especially when we're playing one nighters. We clean it every night.
Had a long thing you clean it out --
Oh yeah. No, I'm talking about, say, you didn't allow any dust and --

If you had to replace cork around the neck, you did that yourself pretty much?

No. We had a special person we could have it done. We only use it so often. Have it done every so often, especially when you're travelling on the road where there's a lot of heat. And wear and tear on the horn. When you get in town, (inaudible) you take your horn down and have the guy to go over it. When you're in Detroit, you take it before you open a theater. You take it to the guy and have him go over it. The guy, you know, they got a special guy that fix horns (inaudible). One time I was playing with Louie, we was out in some town, in Texas somewhere. And the guy dropped the trunk on my horn. And it just knocked (inaudible). It just

knocked it in. So the guy had to strip (inaudible). He took it to a colored fella. He fixed all instruments for the college there. Just happened he had to be there. Took it over that morning and he say, "I'll do it. I'll have it for you tonight." He took all the keys off, took a metal thing down there until he got that horn -- and soft mallet banged it with a (inaudible) until he got that horn -- Never knew if anything happened to it. He put all the keys right back in place. He worked for the -- he fixed all the band instruments for that particular college.

Well once in a while we have trouble with the spring. We carry an extra set of springs ourselves. We used to stick down (inaudible). Because especially when the Selmer summer was easy (inaudible) put a spring on. All you had to do was pull out one and push it up in there, you know.
